title.zh: 卷二百八十 列傳第一百六十八 何騰蛟 瞿式耜
title.en: Volume 280 Biographies 168: He Tengjiao, Ju Shisi

sentences.zh: 何騰蛟

translations.literal: He Tengjiao
translations.idiomatic: He Tengjiao

sentences.zh: 〈（章曠傅作霖）〉

translations.literal: (Zhang Kuang; Fu Zuolin)〉
translations.idiomatic: (see the biographies of Zhang Kuang and Fu Zuolin)〉

sentences.zh: 瞿式耜

translations.literal: Qu Shisi
translations.idiomatic: Qu Shisi

sentences.zh: 〈（汪皞等）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Hao and others)〉
translations.idiomatic: (see the biographies of Wang Hao and others)〉

sentences.zh: 何騰蛟，字雲從，貴州黎平衛人。

translations.literal: He Tengjiao, styled Yuncong, was a native of Liping Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Tengjiao, styled Yuncong, was a native of Liping Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中授南陽知縣。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he was appointed magistrate of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was appointed magistrate of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 地四達，賊出沒其間，數被挫去。

translations.literal: The territory lay at a crossroads; bandits appeared and vanished there, and he drove them off many times.
translations.idiomatic: The district lay at a crossroads where bandits came and went; he repelled them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 已，從巡撫陳必謙破賊安臯山，斬首四百餘級，又討平土寇，益知名。

translations.literal: Later, following Grand Coordinator Chen Biqian, he defeated bandits at Mount Angao, cut off more than four hundred heads, and also pacified local rebels, gaining further renown.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Grand Coordinator Chen Biqian, he defeated bandits at Mount Angao, took more than four hundred heads, and pacified local rebels as well, winning greater fame.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部主事，進員外郎，出為懷來兵備僉事，調口北道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to a clerkship in the Ministry of War, promoted to vice director, and went out as assistant commissioner for military preparations at Huailai; he was then transferred to the Koubei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to a clerkship in the Ministry of War, then vice director, and was appointed assistant commissioner for military preparations at Huailai before transfer to the Koubei circuit.

sentences.zh: 才谞精敏，所在見稱。

translations.literal: Talented, shrewd, and quick, he was praised wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and capable, he won praise wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，巡撫劉永祚薦其賢，乞奪情任事。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Grand Coordinator Liu Yongzuo recommended him for his worth and asked that he leave mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Grand Coordinator Liu Yongzuo praised his merit and asked that he leave mourning to resume office.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟不可，固辭歸。

translations.literal: Tengjiao refused and firmly declined, returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao would not agree and firmly declined, returning home.

sentences.zh: 服除，起淮徐兵備僉事。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was recalled as assistant commissioner for military preparations on the Huai-Xu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was recalled as assistant commissioner for military preparations on the Huai-Xu circuit.

sentences.zh: 討平土寇，部內宴然。

translations.literal: He pacified local bandits, and his jurisdiction was peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified local bandits, and his jurisdiction was at peace.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，拜右僉都御史，代王聚奎巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year, he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and replaced Wang Jukui as Grand Coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and took over from Wang Jukui as grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 時湖北地盡失，止存武昌，屯左良玉大軍，軍橫甚。

translations.literal: At the time the lands of Hubei had all been lost; only Wuchang remained, where Zuo Liangyu's great army was encamped—the army was extremely unruly.
translations.idiomatic: By then northern Huguang had fallen entirely; only Wuchang was left, garrisoned by Zuo Liangyu's main force, whose troops were wildly insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟與良玉交歡，得相安。

translations.literal: Tengjiao and Liangyu became friendly and were able to coexist in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao cultivated good relations with Liangyu, and the two managed to keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣將惠登相、毛憲文復德安、隨州。

translations.literal: The next spring he sent the generals Hu Dengxiang and Mao Xianwen to recover Dean and Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he sent Hu Dengxiang and Mao Xianwen to retake Dean and Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，福王立。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Prince of Fu was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Prince of Fu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔至，良玉駐漢陽，其部下有異議，不欲開讀。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, Liangyu was stationed at Hanyang; his subordinates disputed among themselves and did not wish to open and read it.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial edict arrived, Liangyu was at Hanyang; some of his officers objected and refused to have it read aloud.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟曰：「社稷安危，系此一舉。

translations.literal: Tengjiao said: "The safety of the altars of state and land hinges on this single act.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao said, "The fate of the realm hangs on this one step.

sentences.zh: 倘不奉詔，吾以死殉之。」

translations.literal: If you do not obey the edict, I will die in its service."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not accept the edict, I will die upholding it."

sentences.zh: 抵良玉所，而良玉已聽正紀盧鼎言，開讀如禮。

translations.literal: He went to Liangyu's quarters, but Liangyu had already heeded the counsel of his zhengji Lu Ding and opened and read the edict according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Liangyu's camp, only to find that Liangyu had already taken the advice of his zhengji Lu Ding and received the edict with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 正紀者，良玉所置官名也。

translations.literal: Zhengji was an office title that Liangyu had created.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji was a post title of Liangyu's own invention.

sentences.zh: 八月，福王命加騰蛟兵部右侍郎，兼撫湖南，代李乾德。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Prince of Fu ordered Tengjiao promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and additionally made him Grand Coordinator of Hunan, replacing Li Qiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Prince of Fu promoted him to Right Vice Minister of War with concurrent charge of Hunan, replacing Li Qiande.

sentences.zh: 尋以故官總督湖廣、四川、雲南、貴州、廣西軍務，召總督楊鶚還。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, in his former capacity he was made supreme commander of military affairs in Huguang, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi, and Supreme Commander Yang E was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was confirmed as supreme commander of Huguang, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi, and Yang E was recalled from the post.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，南京有北來太子事，中外以為真，朝臣皆曰偽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year there was the affair of the crown prince who had come from the north at Nanjing; within and without the court most believed him genuine, but the ministers all said he was a fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year Nanjing was stirred by reports of a crown prince arriving from the north; many inside and outside court took him for genuine, while the ministers insisted he was an impostor.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟力言不可殺，與當國者大忤。

translations.literal: Tengjiao strongly argued that he must not be killed and clashed sharply with those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao argued forcefully against executing the man and fell into sharp conflict with the men then directing affairs.

sentences.zh: 無何，良玉舉兵反，邀騰蛟偕行，不可，則盡殺城中人以劫之。

translations.literal: Before long Liangyu raised troops in revolt and invited Tengjiao to go with him; when Tengjiao refused, Liangyu slaughtered everyone in the city to coerce him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liangyu mutinied and urged Tengjiao to join him; when Tengjiao refused, Liangyu massacred the townspeople to force his hand.

sentences.zh: 士民爭匿其署中，騰蛟坐大門縱之入。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners vied to hide in his yamen; Tengjiao sat at the main gate and let them enter.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens rushed to shelter in his compound; Tengjiao sat at the main gate and admitted them all.

sentences.zh: 良玉破垣舉火，避難者悉焚死。

translations.literal: Liangyu breached the walls and set fires; all who had sought refuge were burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's men broke through the walls and set fires, and every refugee inside perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟急解印付家人，令速走，將自剄，為良玉部將擁去。

translations.literal: Tengjiao hastily removed his seal and gave it to a family member, ordering him to flee at once; he was about to cut his own throat when he was seized and carried off by one of Liangyu's subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao quickly handed his seal to a servant and told him to flee, then prepared to take his own life, but was seized and dragged away by one of Liangyu's officers.

sentences.zh: 良玉欲與同舟，不從，乃置之別舟，以副將四人守之。

translations.literal: Liangyu wished him to share the same boat; Tengjiao would not agree, so Liangyu placed him on a separate vessel with four deputy generals to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu wanted him aboard his own boat; when Tengjiao refused, Liangyu put him on another craft with four deputy generals as guards.

sentences.zh: 舟次漢陽門，乘間跌入江水。

translations.literal: When the boat reached the Hanyang Gate, he seized an opening and threw himself into the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: As the boat passed the Hanyang Gate, he seized a moment's chance and plunged into the river.

sentences.zh: 四人懼誅，亦赴水。

translations.literal: The four men, fearing execution, also threw themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The four guards, fearing punishment, jumped in after him.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟漂十餘里，漁舟救之起，則漢前將軍關壯繆侯廟前也。

translations.literal: Tengjiao drifted more than ten li before a fishing boat pulled him out—it was in front of the temple of Marquis Zhuangmou, the Han-era General Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao drifted more than ten li before fishermen hauled him ashore—directly before the shrine of Marquis Zhuangmou, the Han general Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 家人懷印者亦至，相視大驚。

translations.literal: The family member carrying the seal also arrived; they looked at each other in great astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: The servant bearing his seal arrived as well, and the two stared at each other in amazement.

sentences.zh: 覓漁舟，忽不見。

translations.literal: They looked for the fishing boat, but it had suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: They searched for the fishing boat, but it had vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 遠近謂騰蛟忠誠得神佑，益歸心焉。

translations.literal: Near and far people said Tengjiao's loyalty had won divine protection, and they devoted themselves to him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: People far and near took it as proof that Tengjiao's loyalty had won heaven's protection, and their hearts turned to him all the more.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟乃從寧州轉瀏陽，抵長沙。

translations.literal: Tengjiao then went from Ningzhou by way of Liuyang and reached Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao made his way from Ningzhou through Liuyang to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 集諸屬吏堵胤錫、傅上瑞、嚴起恒、章曠、周大啟、吳晉錫等，痛哭盟誓。

translations.literal: He gathered his subordinate officials Du Yinxie, Fu Shangrui, Yan Qiheng, Zhang Kuang, Zhou Daqi, Wu Jinxi, and others, and with weeping they swore a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered his lieutenants—Du Yinxie, Fu Shangrui, Yan Qiheng, Zhang Kuang, Zhou Daqi, Wu Jinxi, and the rest—and they wept as they swore a solemn oath.

sentences.zh: 分士馬舟艦糗糧，各任其一。

translations.literal: They divided troops, horses, boats, warships, and provisions, each man taking charge of one part.
translations.idiomatic: They divided men, horses, boats, grain, and supplies, each taking responsibility for one branch of the effort.

sentences.zh: 令胤錫攝湖北巡撫，上瑞攝湖南巡撫，曠為總督監軍，大啟提督學政。

translations.literal: He ordered Yinxie to act as Grand Coordinator of Hubei, Shangrui to act as Grand Coordinator of Hunan, Kuang to serve as the supreme commander's army supervisor, and Daqi to supervise education in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yinxie in charge of Hubei as acting grand coordinator, Shangrui in charge of Hunan, made Kuang army supervisor under the supreme commander, and appointed Daqi provincial education intendant.

sentences.zh: 起恒故衡永道，即督二郡軍食，晉錫以長沙推官攝郴桂道事。

translations.literal: Qiheng had formerly been intendant of the Heng-Yong circuit and now supervised military provisions for the two prefectures; Jinxi, as Changsha's magistrate-adjunct, acted in charge of the Chen-Gui circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng, formerly intendant of the Hengzhou-Yongzhou circuit, now oversaw provisions for both prefectures; Jinxi, as acting magistrate of Changsha, took charge of the Chenzhou-Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 即遣曠調副將黃朝宣、張先璧、劉承胤兵。

translations.literal: He immediately sent Kuang to summon the troops of the deputy generals Huang Chaoxuan, Zhang Xianbi, and Liu Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: He at once dispatched Kuang to rally the forces of deputy generals Huang Chaoxuan, Zhang Xianbi, and Liu Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 朝宣自燕子窩，先璧自漵浦，承胤自武岡，先後至，兵勢稍振。

translations.literal: Chaoxuan came from Yanziwuo, Xianbi from Xupu, and Chengyin from Wugang; they arrived one after another and military strength revived somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxuan marched from Yanziwuo, Xianbi from Xupu, and Chengyin from Wugang; as they arrived in turn, the army's strength began to recover.

sentences.zh: 而是時良玉已死。

translations.literal: But by this time Liangyu was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, Liangyu was already dead.

sentences.zh: 順治二年五月，大兵下南都。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi the great army took the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi the Qing armies captured Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 唐王聿鍵自立於福州。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince Zhu Yujian declared himself ruler at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince Zhu Yujian proclaimed himself emperor at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王居南陽時，素知騰蛟賢，委任益至。

translations.literal: When the prince had lived at Nanyang he had long known Tengjiao's worth and now entrusted him all the more fully.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had known Tengjiao's worth since his days at Nanyang and now relied on him more than ever.

sentences.zh: 李自成斃於九宮山，其將劉體仁、郝搖旗等以眾無主，議歸騰蛟。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng had died at Jiugong Mountain; his generals Liu Tiren, Hao Yaoqi, and others, finding their forces without a leader, deliberated submitting to Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had died on Jiugong Mountain; his generals Liu Tiren, Hao Yaoqi, and others, leaderless, resolved to submit to Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 率四五萬人驟入湘陰，距長沙百餘里。

translations.literal: They led forty or fifty thousand men in a sudden advance into Xiangyin, little more than a hundred li from Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: They marched forty or fifty thousand men in a sudden thrust into Xiangyin, barely a hundred li from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 城中人不知其求歸也，懼甚。

translations.literal: The people in the city did not know they had come to submit and were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The city did not know they had come to surrender, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 朝宣即引兵還燕子窩。

translations.literal: Chaoxuan at once led his troops back to Yanziwuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxuan immediately withdrew his troops to Yanziwuo.

sentences.zh: 上瑞請騰蛟出避，騰蛟曰：「死於左，死於賊，一也，何避焉。」

translations.literal: Shangrui asked Tengjiao to flee; Tengjiao said: "To die at the hands of Zuo or to die at the hands of bandits is all one—why flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangrui urged Tengjiao to flee; Tengjiao replied, "Death at Zuo's hands or death at the rebels' hands is all the same—why should I run?"

sentences.zh: 長沙知府周二南請往偵之，以千人護行。

translations.literal: The prefect of Changsha, Zhou Ernan, asked to go and reconnoiter them, with a thousand men as escort.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Changsha, Zhou Ernan, volunteered to scout them out, escorted by a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賊謂其迎敵也，射殺之，從行者盡死。

translations.literal: The bandits thought he had come to fight them and shot him dead; all who accompanied him were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took them for an attacking force and shot Zhou dead; every man in the party was killed.

sentences.zh: 城中益懼，士女悉竄。

translations.literal: Fear in the city grew worse; men and women all fled in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Panic in the city deepened, and the populace scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟與曠謀，遣部將萬大鵬等二人往撫。

translations.literal: Tengjiao consulted with Kuang and sent two subordinate generals, Wan Dapeng and another, to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao and Kuang devised a plan and sent two officers, Wan Dapeng among them, to treat with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊見止二騎，迎入演武場，飲之酒。

translations.literal: The bandits saw only two horsemen and welcomed them into the drill ground, offering them wine.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing only two riders, the rebels welcomed them to the drill ground and offered wine.

sentences.zh: 二人不交一言，與痛飲。

translations.literal: The two men exchanged not a word and drank heavily with them.
translations.idiomatic: The two envoys said nothing and drank deeply with them.

sentences.zh: 飲畢，賊問來意，答言督師以湘陰褊小，不足容大軍，請即移長沙。

translations.literal: When the drinking was finished the bandits asked their purpose; they answered that the supreme commander said Xiangyin was too cramped to hold a great army and asked them to move at once to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When the cups were empty the rebels asked their errand; they replied that the supreme commander found Xiangyin too cramped for so large a host and invited them to move straight to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 因致騰蛟手書召之曰：「公等歸朝，誓永保富貴。」

translations.literal: They also delivered a letter in Tengjiao's own hand summoning them: "When you gentlemen return to the dynasty, I swear you shall forever enjoy wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: They presented Tengjiao's own letter, which read: "Once you return to the cause, I pledge that wealth and rank shall be yours forever."

sentences.zh: 搖旗等大喜，與大鵬至長沙。

translations.literal: Yaoqi and the others were greatly pleased and went with Dapeng to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqi and his fellows were overjoyed and marched with Dapeng to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟開誠撫慰，宴飲盡歡，犒從官牛酒。

translations.literal: Tengjiao received them with open sincerity and comforted them; they feasted and drank to the full, and he rewarded their officers with beef and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao received them with frank goodwill, feasted them generously, and rewarded their officers with beef and wine.

sentences.zh: 命先璧以卒三萬馳射，旌旗蔽天。

translations.literal: He ordered Xianbi to have thirty thousand troops perform mounted archery; banners and flags blotted out the sky.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xianbi put thirty thousand men through cavalry drills until banners darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 搖旗等大悅，招其黨袁宗第、藺養成、王進才、牛有勇皆來歸，驟增兵十余萬，聲威大震。

translations.literal: Yaoqi and the others were greatly delighted; they summoned their comrades Yuan Zongdi, Lan Yangcheng, Wang Jincai, and Niu Youyong, who all came to submit, and in a sudden surge their forces increased by more than a hundred thousand; their prestige shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Yaoqi called in his comrades Yuan Zongdi, Lan Yangcheng, Wang Jincai, and Niu Youyong, and as they all submitted his army swelled by more than a hundred thousand men and his fame resounded across the land.

sentences.zh: 未幾，自成將李錦、高必正擁眾數十萬逼常德。

translations.literal: Before long Zicheng's generals Li Jin and Gao Bizheng, leading several hundred thousand men, pressed upon Changde.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zicheng's generals Li Jin and Gao Bizheng advanced on Changde with several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟令胤錫撫降之，置之荊州。

translations.literal: Tengjiao ordered Yinxie to pacify them into surrender and stationed them at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao sent Yinxie to accept their surrender and quartered them at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦，自成從子，後賜名赤心。

translations.literal: Jin was Zicheng's nephew by marriage and was later granted the name Chixin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was Zicheng's nephew and was later given the name Chixin, "Red Heart."

sentences.zh: 必正則自成妻高氏弟也。

translations.literal: Bizheng was the younger brother of Zicheng's wife, the Lady Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Bizheng was the younger brother of Zicheng's wife, Lady Gao.

sentences.zh: 高氏語錦曰：「汝願為無賴賊，抑願為大將邪？」

translations.literal: Lady Gao said to Jin: "Do you wish to remain a worthless bandit, or do you wish to be a great general?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao said to Jin, "Do you mean to stay a common brigand, or do you mean to become a true commander?"

sentences.zh: 錦曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: Jin said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin asked, "What do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「為賊無論，既以身許國，當愛民，受主將節制，有死無二，吾所願也。」

translations.literal: She said: "As for being a bandit, that goes without saying; now that you have pledged your person to the state, you ought to cherish the people, accept the supreme commander's discipline, and die without a second thought—that is what I desire."
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "Never mind the past as a rebel—now that you have pledged yourself to the dynasty, you must cherish the people, obey your commander, and die if need be without wavering. That is what I want of you."

sentences.zh: 錦曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "I agree."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "It shall be so."

sentences.zh: 騰蛟慮錦跋扈，他日過其營，請見高氏，再拜，執禮恭。

translations.literal: Tengjiao, fearing Jin's arrogance, one day visited his camp and asked to see Lady Gao; he bowed twice and observed the rites with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jin's unruliness, Tengjiao one day visited his camp, asked to see Lady Gao, bowed deeply, and treated her with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 高氏悅，戒其子毋忘何公，錦自是無異志。

translations.literal: Lady Gao was pleased and admonished her son not to forget Lord He; from then on Jin harbored no other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao was pleased and warned her son never to forget Lord He; from that day Jin gave no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 自成亂天下二十年，陷帝都，覆廟社，其眾數十萬悉歸騰蛟。

translations.literal: Zicheng had thrown the realm into chaos for twenty years, seized the imperial capital, and overturned the altars of state and land; his forces, several hundred thousand strong, all submitted to Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng had ravaged the empire for twenty years, seized the capital, and toppled the dynasty; yet his hosts, several hundred thousand strong, now submitted entirely to Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 而騰蛟上疏，但言元兇已除，稍泄神人憤，宜告謝郊廟，卒不言己功。

translations.literal: Yet in his memorial Tengjiao spoke only of how the arch-criminal had been removed and how the wrath of spirits and men was somewhat relieved, and that thanksgiving ought to be offered at the suburban altars—he never mentioned his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial Tengjiao spoke only of the arch-rebel's removal and the easing of heaven's and men's wrath, urging thanksgiving at the suburban altars—and said nothing of his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 唐王大喜，立拜東閣大學士兼兵部尚書，封定興伯，仍督師。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince was greatly pleased and at once appointed him Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrently Minister of War, enfeoffing him as Earl of Dingxing while he continued as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince was overjoyed, made him Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and Minister of War, enfeoffed him as Earl of Dingxing, and left him in command.

sentences.zh: 而疑自成死未實。

translations.literal: Yet he doubted whether Zicheng's death was truly established.
translations.idiomatic: He still doubted whether Zicheng was truly dead.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟言自成定死，身首已糜爛。

translations.literal: Tengjiao said Zicheng was certainly dead and that body and head had already rotted away.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao assured him that Zicheng was dead beyond doubt, his body already decayed beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 不敢居功，因固辭封爵。

translations.literal: He did not dare claim merit and therefore firmly declined enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to claim credit, he firmly declined the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 不允，令規取江西及南都。

translations.literal: The prince would not agree and ordered him to plan the recovery of Jiangxi and the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The refusal was not accepted, and he was ordered to plan the reconquest of Jiangxi and Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 當是時，降卒既眾，騰蛟欲以舊軍參之，乃題授朝宣、先璧為總兵官，與承胤、赤心、郝永忠、宗第、進才及董英、馬進忠、馬士秀、曹誌建、王允成、盧鼎並開鎮湖南、北，時所謂十三鎮者也。

translations.literal: At this time the surrendered troops were already numerous; Tengjiao wished to mix in the old armies with them and therefore appointed Chaoxuan and Xianbi regional commanders-in-chief, and together with Chengyin, Chixin, Hao Yongzhong, Zongdi, Jincai, and also Dong Ying, Ma Jinzhong, Ma Shixiu, Cao Zhijian, Wang Yuncheng, and Lu Ding opened garrisons across Hunan north and south—the so-called Thirteen Garrisons of the time.
translations.idiomatic: With so many surrendered troops, Tengjiao sought to blend them with his older forces and appointed Chaoxuan and Xianbi regional commanders, along with Chengyin, Chixin, Hao Yongzhong, Zongdi, Jincai, Dong Ying, Ma Jinzhong, Ma Shixiu, Cao Zhijian, Wang Yuncheng, and Lu Ding, establishing garrisons across Hunan—the famous Thirteen Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 永忠即搖旗，英，騰蛟中軍，誌建則故巡按劉熙祚中軍，余皆良玉舊將也。

translations.literal: Yongzhong was Yaoqi; Ying was Tengjiao's central army commander; Zhijian had been the central army commander of the former touring censor Liu Xizuo; the rest were all Liangyu's old generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong was Yaoqi; Ying commanded Tengjiao's personal guard; Zhijian had served the touring censor Liu Xizuo; the rest were Zuo Liangyu's former officers.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟銳意東下，拜表出師。

translations.literal: Tengjiao was keen to drive eastward and submitted a memorial to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to advance eastward, Tengjiao memorialized the throne and marched out.

sentences.zh: 明年正月與監軍御史李膺品先赴湘陰，期大會岳州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he and the army-supervising censor Li Yingpin went first to Xiangyin, arranging a great rendezvous at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he and the army supervisor Li Yingpin went ahead to Xiangyin, planning a general muster at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 先璧逗遛，諸營亦觀望，獨赤心自湖北至，為大兵所敗而還，諸鎮兵遂罷，騰蛟威望由此損。

translations.literal: Xianbi lingered; the other camps also watched and waited; only Chixin came from Hubei, was defeated by the great army and retreated, and the troops of the various garrisons then dispersed; Tengjiao's prestige was thereby diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi dallied, the other camps held back, and only Chixin marched down from Hubei—only to be beaten back by the Qing forces. The campaign collapsed, and Tengjiao's authority never recovered.

sentences.zh: 時諸將皆驕且貪殘，朝宣尤甚，劫人而剝其皮。

translations.literal: At the time the generals were all arrogant and greedy and cruel; Chaoxuan was worst of all, seizing people and flaying off their skin.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had grown arrogant and rapacious; Chaoxuan was the worst, robbing captives and flaying them alive.

sentences.zh: 永忠效之，殺民無虛日。

translations.literal: Yongzhong imitated him and killed civilians not a day without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong followed his example, and scarcely a day passed without civilians being killed.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟不能制。

translations.literal: Tengjiao could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 故總督楊鶚者，克餉失軍心，至是復夤緣為偏沅總督。

translations.literal: The former supreme commander Yang E, who had withheld pay and lost the army's loyalty, now by backdoor influence again became supreme commander of western Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang E, the former supreme commander who had withheld pay and lost the troops' loyalty, now maneuvered his way back into office as commander of western Hunan.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟以為言，乃召鶚還。

translations.literal: Tengjiao spoke against it, and Yang E was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao protested, and Yang E was recalled.

sentences.zh: 王數議出關，為鄭氏所阻。

translations.literal: The prince repeatedly discussed moving out of Fujian, but was blocked by the Zheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: The prince often debated marching north from Fujian, but the Zheng clan blocked him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟屢請幸贛，協力取江西。

translations.literal: Tengjiao repeatedly asked that the prince proceed to Ganzhou and join forces to recover Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao repeatedly urged the prince to move to Ganzhou and join him in retaking Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 王遣使征兵，騰蛟發永忠精騎五千往。

translations.literal: The prince sent envoys to levy troops; Tengjiao dispatched five thousand of Yongzhong's elite cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent to levy troops, and Tengjiao dispatched five thousand of Yongzhong's best horsemen.

sentences.zh: 永忠不肯前，五月始抵郴州。

translations.literal: Yongzhong refused to advance and only in the fifth month reached Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong refused to march until the fifth month, when he finally reached Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 會大兵破汀州，聿鍵被執死，贛州亦失。

translations.literal: Just then the great army took Tingzhou; Yujian was captured and killed, and Ganzhou was also lost.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qing armies had taken Tingzhou; Yujian was captured and executed, and Ganzhou fell as well.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟聞王死，大慟，厲兵保境如平時。

translations.literal: When Tengjiao heard of the prince's death he grieved greatly, yet drilled his troops and guarded his territory as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the prince's death, Tengjiao mourned deeply, yet drilled his troops and held his territory as steadfastly as before.

sentences.zh: 已，聞永明王立，乃稍自安。

translations.literal: Later, when he heard the Yongli Prince had been enthroned, he was somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he learned that the Yongli Emperor had been enthroned, he took some comfort.

sentences.zh: 王尋以騰蛟為武英殿大學士，加太子太保。

translations.literal: The prince soon made Tengjiao Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence and added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王進才故守益陽，聞大兵漸逼，還長沙。

translations.literal: Wang Jincai had been holding Yiyang; hearing that the great army was drawing near, he returned to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jincai, who had been defending Yiyang, withdrew to Changsha as the Qing armies closed in.

sentences.zh: 四年春，進才揚言乏餉，大掠，並及湘陰。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year Jincai claimed a shortage of pay and carried out great pillaging, extending even to Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year Jincai pleaded shortage of supplies and plundered widely, even raiding Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 適大兵至長沙，進才走湖北。

translations.literal: Just then the great army reached Changsha; Jincai fled to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qing forces reached Changsha, Jincai fled into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟不能守，單騎走衡州，長沙、湘陰並失。

translations.literal: Tengjiao could not hold the city and fled alone on horseback to Hengzhou; Changsha and Xiangyin were both lost.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to hold the city, Tengjiao fled alone to Hengzhou; Changsha and Xiangyin both fell.

sentences.zh: 盧鼎時守衡州，而先璧兵突至，大掠。

translations.literal: Lu Ding was then defending Hengzhou, but Xianbi's troops suddenly arrived and carried out great pillaging.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ding was defending Hengzhou when Xianbi's troops burst in and plundered the city.

sentences.zh: 鼎不能抗，走永州。

translations.literal: Ding could not resist and fled to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to resist, Ding withdrew to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先璧遂挾騰蛟走祁陽，又間道走辰州。

translations.literal: Xianbi then seized Tengjiao and fled with him to Qiyang, then by a hidden route to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi then seized Tengjiao and fled with him to Qiyang, then by back roads toward Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟脫還，走永州。

translations.literal: Tengjiao escaped and returned, fleeing to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao broke free and fled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 甫至，鼎部將復大掠。

translations.literal: He had barely arrived when Ding's subordinate generals again carried out great pillaging.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived when Lu Ding's officers looted the city again.

sentences.zh: 鼎走道州，騰蛟與侍郎嚴起恒走白牙市，大兵遂下衡、永。

translations.literal: Ding fled to Daozhou; Tengjiao and Vice Minister Yan Qiheng fled to Baiya Market, and the great army then took Hengzhou and Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding fled to Daozhou; Tengjiao and Vice Minister Yan Qiheng withdrew to Baiya, and the Qing armies overran Hengzhou and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，騰蛟建十三鎮以衛長沙，至是皆自為盜賊。

translations.literal: At first Tengjiao had established the Thirteen Garrisons to defend Changsha; by now they had all become bandits in their own right.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao had once raised the Thirteen Garrisons to shield Changsha; now they had all turned into freebooters.

sentences.zh: 大兵入衡州，守將黃朝宣降。

translations.literal: When the great army entered Hengzhou, the defending general Huang Chaoxuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing forces entered Hengzhou, the garrison commander Huang Chaoxuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 數其罪，支解之，遠近大快。

translations.literal: They enumerated his crimes and dismembered him; near and far rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They recited his crimes and had him torn limb from limb, to universal satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 大清以一知府守永州，副將周金湯間城虛，夜鼓噪而登，知府出走，金湯遂入永。

translations.literal: The Great Qing left one prefect to hold Yongzhou; Deputy General Zhou Jintang, finding the city weakly defended, at night raised a clamor and scaled the walls; the prefect fled, and Jintang then entered Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing left a single prefect to hold Yongzhou; Deputy General Zhou Jintang found the defenses thin, stormed the walls by night with a great din, and took the city as the prefect fled.

sentences.zh: 六月，騰蛟在白牙。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tengjiao was at Baiya.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Tengjiao was at Baiya.

sentences.zh: 王密遣中使告以劉承胤罪，令入武岡除之。

translations.literal: The prince secretly sent a palace envoy to report Liu Chengyin's crimes and ordered Tengjiao to enter Wugang and eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent a palace envoy to report Liu Chengyin's crimes and ordered Tengjiao into Wugang to remove him.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟乃走謁王，王及太后皆召見。

translations.literal: Tengjiao then went in haste to pay court to the prince; both the prince and the empress dowager summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao hurried to court; both the emperor and the empress dowager received him in audience.

sentences.zh: 承胤由小校，以騰蛟薦至大將，已漸倨。

translations.literal: Chengyin had risen from a petty officer through Tengjiao's recommendation to great general and had already grown gradually arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin had risen from a petty officer on Tengjiao's recommendation to full general, and had grown increasingly insolent.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟在長沙征其兵，承胤大怒，言：「先調朝宣、先璧軍，皆章曠親行，今乃折箠使我。」

translations.literal: When Tengjiao at Changsha levied troops from him, Chengyin was greatly angered and said: "When Chaoxuan's and Xianbi's armies were first called up, Zhang Kuang went in person; now you crack a whip to drive me."
translations.idiomatic: When Tengjiao at Changsha demanded his troops, Chengyin flew into a rage and said, "When Chaoxuan and Xianbi were first mobilized, Zhang Kuang went in person—yet now you crack a whip at me."

sentences.zh: 遂馳至黎平，執騰蛟子，索餉數萬。

translations.literal: He then galloped to Liping, seized Tengjiao's son, and demanded tens of thousands in pay.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to Liping, seized Tengjiao's son, and demanded tens of thousands in silver for supplies.

sentences.zh: 子走訴騰蛟，騰蛟遣曠行，承胤乃以眾至。

translations.literal: The son fled to tell Tengjiao; Tengjiao sent Kuang to go, and Chengyin then came with his host.
translations.idiomatic: The son fled to Tengjiao, who sent Zhang Kuang to negotiate; Chengyin then marched in with his army.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟為請於王，得封定蠻伯，且與為姻，承胤益驕。

translations.literal: Tengjiao pleaded with the prince on his behalf; he was enfeoffed as Earl Who Pacifies the Man, and a marriage alliance was made as well; Chengyin grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao interceded with the court; Chengyin was enfeoffed Earl Who Pacifies the Man and given a marriage tie to the throne, and grew still more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 至是爵安國公，勛上柱國，賜尚方劍，益坐大。

translations.literal: By now he was ennobled Duke of Pacifying the State, made Pillar of the State of the First Order, and granted the Imperial Sword; he sat even larger in his pride.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had been made Duke of Pacifying the State, Pillar of the State of the First Order, and granted the Imperial Sword—and his arrogance knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 忌騰蛟出己上，欲奪其權，請用為戶部尚書，專領餉務，王不許。

translations.literal: Jealous that Tengjiao stood above him, he wished to seize his power and asked that Tengjiao be used as Minister of Revenue to oversee pay alone; the prince would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting Tengjiao's seniority, he sought to strip him of command and proposed making him Minister of Revenue in charge of supplies alone; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 王召騰蛟圖承胤，騰蛟無兵，命以雲南援將趙印選、胡一青兵隸之。

translations.literal: The prince summoned Tengjiao to plan against Chengyin; Tengjiao had no troops and was ordered to place under his command the Yunnan relief generals Zhao Yinxuan and Hu Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Tengjiao to deal with Chengyin; lacking troops of his own, Tengjiao was given the Yunnan relief generals Zhao Yinxuan and Hu Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 及辭朝，賜銀幣，命廷臣郊餞。

translations.literal: When he took leave of court he was granted silver and silks, and the court ministers were ordered to give him a suburban farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving court he was rewarded with silver and silks, and the ministers were ordered to see him off with a suburban feast.

sentences.zh: 承胤伏千騎襲騰蛟，印選卒力戰，盡殲之，騰蛟乃還駐白牙。

translations.literal: Chengyin lay in ambush with a thousand horsemen to attack Tengjiao; Yinxuan's troops fought fiercely and annihilated them all; Tengjiao then returned to garrison Baiya.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin ambushed him with a thousand horsemen; Yinxuan's men fought fiercely and wiped them out, and Tengjiao returned to Baiya.

sentences.zh: 八月，大兵破武岡，承胤降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the great army took Wugang and Chengyin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Qing armies took Wugang and Chengyin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王走靖州，又走柳州。

translations.literal: The prince fled to Jingzhou, then again to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Jingzhou, then on to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時常德、寶慶已失，永亦再失。

translations.literal: By then Changde and Baoqing had already been lost, and Yong had been lost a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Changde and Baoqing had already fallen, and Yongzhou had been lost again.

sentences.zh: 王將返桂林，而城中止焦璉軍，騰蛟率印選、一青入為助。

translations.literal: The prince was about to return to Guilin, but in the city there was only Jiao Lian's army; Tengjiao led Yinxuan and Yiqing in to assist.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to return to Guilin, only Jiao Lian's troops held the city; Tengjiao led Yinxuan and Yiqing in to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 而南安侯郝永忠忽擁眾萬余至，與璉兵欲鬥，會宜章伯盧鼎兵亦至，騰蛟為調劑，桂林以安。

translations.literal: But the Nan'an Marquis Hao Yongzhong suddenly arrived leading more than ten thousand men and was about to fight with Lian's troops; then the Yizhang Earl Lu Ding's army also came, and Tengjiao mediated between them so that Guilin was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Then Nan'an Marquis Hao Yongzhong suddenly arrived with more than ten thousand men and nearly clashed with Jiao Lian's troops; when Yizhang Earl Lu Ding's force also appeared, Tengjiao mediated between them and Guilin was spared.

sentences.zh: 乃遣璉、永忠、鼎、印選、一青分扼興安、靈川、永寧、義寧諸州縣。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Lian, Yongzhong, Ding, Yinxuan, and Yiqing to hold separately the prefectures and counties of Xing'an, Lingchuan, Yongning, and Yining.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Lian, Yongzhong, Ding, Yinxuan, and Yiqing to hold Xing'an, Lingchuan, Yongning, and Yining.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大兵逼全州，騰蛟督五將合禦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the great army pressed upon Quanzhou; Tengjiao supervised the five generals in combined defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Qing armies pressed Quanzhou, and Tengjiao directed five generals in a united defense.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，王居桂林，加騰蛟太師，進爵為侯，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the prince resided at Guilin; Tengjiao was made Grand Preceptor, advanced in rank to marquis with hereditary succession for his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, with the court at Guilin, Tengjiao was made Grand Preceptor, raised to marquis with hereditary rank for his line.

sentences.zh: 二月，大兵破全州，至興安。

translations.literal: In the second month the great army took Quanzhou and reached Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Qing forces took Quanzhou and advanced to Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 永忠兵大潰，奔桂林，逼王西，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: Yongzhong's army collapsed in great rout, fled to Guilin, pressed the prince westward, and let his troops pillage on a vast scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong's army collapsed and fled to Guilin, driving the emperor westward while his men looted the city.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟自永福至。

translations.literal: Tengjiao came from Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao hurried up from Yongfu.

sentences.zh: 大兵知桂林有變，直抵北門。

translations.literal: The great army, learning that Guilin was in turmoil, went straight to the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the turmoil in Guilin, the Qing army marched straight to the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟督璉、一青等分三門拒守，大兵乃還全州。

translations.literal: Tengjiao directed Lian, Yiqing, and the others to defend the three gates separately, and the great army then withdrew to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao directed Jiao Lian, Hu Yiqing, and the others to hold the three gates, and the Qing forces withdrew to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會金聲桓、李成棟叛大清，以兵附。

translations.literal: Just then Jin Shengheng and Li Chengdong rebelled against the Great Qing and attached their armies to the Southern Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Jin Shengheng and Li Chengdong rebelled against the Qing and brought their armies over to the Southern Ming.

sentences.zh: 大兵在湖南者姑退，騰蛟遂取全州。

translations.literal: The great army in Hunan for the time being withdrew, and Tengjiao then recovered Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing forces in Hunan temporarily withdrew, and Tengjiao retook Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復遣保昌侯曹誌建、宜章侯盧鼎、新興侯焦璉、新寧侯趙印選攻永州，圍城三月，大小三十六戰，十一月朔克之。

translations.literal: He again sent the Baochang Marquis Cao Zhijian, the Yizhang Marquis Lu Ding, the Xinxing Marquis Jiao Lian, and the Xinning Marquis Zhao Yinxuan to attack Yongzhou; they besieged the city three months, fought thirty-six battles great and small, and on the first day of the eleventh month took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Baochang Marquis Cao Zhijian, Yizhang Marquis Lu Ding, Xinxing Marquis Jiao Lian, and Xinning Marquis Zhao Yinxuan against Yongzhou; after a three-month siege and thirty-six engagements they took the city on the first day of the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 未幾，監軍御史余鯤起、職方主事李甲春取寶慶，諸將亦取衡州，馬進忠取常德，所失地多復。

translations.literal: Before long the army-supervising censor Yu Kunqi and the Bureau of Appointments director Li Jiachun took Baoqing; the other generals also took Hengzhou, Ma Jinzhong took Changde, and much of the lost territory was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the army supervisor Yu Kunqi and Bureau director Li Jiachun retook Baoqing; other generals recovered Hengzhou, Ma Jinzhong retook Changde, and much lost ground was won back.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟議進兵長沙。

translations.literal: Tengjiao proposed advancing on Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao proposed marching on Changsha.

sentences.zh: 會督師堵胤錫惡進忠，招忠貞營李赤心軍自夔州至，令進忠讓常德與之。

translations.literal: But the supreme commander Du Yinxie disliked Jinzhong and summoned the Loyal-and-Faithful Battalion army of Li Chixin from Kuizhou, ordering Jinzhong to yield Changde to them.
translations.idiomatic: But supreme commander Du Yinxie disliked Jinzhong and brought Li Chixin's Loyal-and-Faithful Battalion down from Kuizhou, ordering Jinzhong to yield Changde to them.

sentences.zh: 進忠大怒，盡驅居民出城，焚廬舍，走武岡。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was greatly enraged, drove all the inhabitants out of the city, burned the houses, and fled to Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Jinzhong drove the populace from the city, burned the buildings, and fled to Wugang.

sentences.zh: 寶慶守將王進才亦棄城走，他守將皆潰。

translations.literal: The Baoqing garrison commander Wang Jincai also abandoned the city and fled; the other defending generals all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jincai, defending Baoqing, also abandoned his post, and the other garrisons broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 赤心等所至皆空城，旋棄走，東趨長沙。

translations.literal: Wherever Chixin and the others went they found only empty cities; they soon abandoned them and fled east toward Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Chixin's men found only empty cities wherever they went; they soon abandoned them and marched east toward Changsha.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟時駐衡州，大駭。

translations.literal: Tengjiao was then stationed at Hengzhou and was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao, then at Hengzhou, was appalled.

sentences.zh: 六年正月檄進忠由益陽出長沙，期諸將畢會，而親詣忠貞營，邀赤心入衡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he issued orders to Jinzhong to come out from Yiyang toward Changsha, fixing a date for all the generals to assemble, while he himself went to the Loyal-and-Faithful camp to invite Chixin into Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he ordered Jinzhong out from Yiyang toward Changsha, set a rendezvous for all his generals, and went in person to the Loyal-and-Faithful camp to lure Chixin into Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 部下卒六千人，懼忠貞營掩襲，不護行，止攜吏卒三十人往。

translations.literal: His subordinates numbered six thousand troops; fearing an ambush by the Loyal-and-Faithful camp, they would not escort him and he took only thirty clerks and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His six thousand troops feared an ambush from the Loyal-and-Faithful camp and refused to escort him; he went with only thirty clerks and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 將至，聞其軍已東，即尾之至湘潭。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive he heard their army had already gone east; he followed in their wake to Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he learned the army had already marched east; he followed them to Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 湘潭空城也，赤心不守而去，騰蛟乃入居之。

translations.literal: Xiangtan was an empty city; Chixin did not hold it and departed, and Tengjiao then entered and took up residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangtan was deserted; Chixin had passed through without garrisoning it, and Tengjiao moved in.

sentences.zh: 大兵知騰蛟入空城，遣將徐勇引軍入。

translations.literal: The great army, learning that Tengjiao had entered the empty city, sent the general Xu Yong to lead troops in.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Tengjiao had entered the empty city, the Qing sent General Xu Yong in with his troops.

sentences.zh: 勇，騰蛟舊部將也，率其卒羅拜，勸騰蛟降。

translations.literal: Yong had been Tengjiao's old subordinate general; he led his soldiers in a ring of prostration and urged Tengjiao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yong had once served under Tengjiao; his men prostrated themselves in a circle and urged Tengjiao to submit.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟大叱，勇遂擁之去。

translations.literal: Tengjiao shouted him down sharply; Yong then seized him and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao rebuked him fiercely; Yong then seized him and carried him away.

sentences.zh: 絕食七日，乃殺之。

translations.literal: He fasted seven days, and then they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused food for seven days, and then they executed him.

sentences.zh: 永明王聞之哀悼，賜祭者九，贈中湘王，謚文烈，官其子文瑞僉都御史。

translations.literal: When the Yongli Prince heard of it he mourned deeply, granted nine funerary offerings, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongxiang with the temple name Wenlie, and appointed his son Wenrui Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongli Emperor mourned him deeply, granted nine funerary offerings, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Zhongxiang with the posthumous name Wenlie, and appointed his son Wenrui Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 章曠，字於野，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kuang, courtesy name Yuye, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kuang, courtesy name Yuye, came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the tenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the tenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授沔陽知州。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，賊將郝搖旗陷其城，同知馬飆死之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year the bandit general Hao Yaoqi took his city; the vice magistrate Ma Piao died in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year the rebel general Hao Yaoqi captured the city; Vice Magistrate Ma Piao died defending it.

sentences.zh: 曠走免，謁總督袁繼鹹於九江，署為監紀。

translations.literal: Kuang fled and escaped, called on Supreme Commander Yuan Jixian at Jiujiang, and was appointed acting army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang escaped, presented himself to Supreme Commander Yuan Jixian at Jiujiang, and was made acting army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 從諸將方國安、毛憲文、馬進忠、王允成等復漢陽。

translations.literal: He followed the generals Fang Guo'an, Mao Xianwen, Ma Jinzhong, Wang Yuncheng, and others in recovering Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fang Guo'an, Mao Xianwen, Ma Jinzhong, Wang Yuncheng, and others in retaking Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 武昌巡按御史黃澍令署漢陽推官兼攝府事，承德巡撫王揚基令署分巡道事。

translations.literal: The Wuchang touring censor Huang Shu ordered him to act as Hanyang magistrate-adjunct while also overseeing prefectural affairs; the Chengde grand coordinator Wang Yangji ordered him to act as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang touring censor Huang Shu put him in charge of Hanyang as acting magistrate-adjunct and prefectural affairs; Chengde grand coordinator Wang Yangji made him acting circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，憲文偕惠登相復德安，揚基檄曠往守。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year Xianwen together with Hu Dengxiang recovered Dean; Yangji ordered Kuang to go and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month Xianwen and Hu Dengxiang retook Dean, and Yangji ordered Kuang to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 城空無人，衛官十數人賫印送賊將白旺。

translations.literal: The city was empty of people; a dozen or so guard officers carried the seal and presented it to the bandit general Bai Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The city was deserted; a dozen guard officers carried the seal and surrendered it to the rebel general Bai Wang.

sentences.zh: 曠收斬之，日夕為警備。

translations.literal: Kuang seized and executed them, and from morning to night made preparations against attack.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang seized and executed them, then worked day and night to ready the defenses.

sentences.zh: 居三月，代者李藻至，巡撫何騰蛟檄曠署荊西道事。

translations.literal: After three months his replacement Li Zao arrived; Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao ordered Kuang to act in charge of the Jingxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After three months his replacement Li Zao arrived; Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao appointed Kuang acting intendant of the Jingxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 曠去，藻失將士心，城復陷。

translations.literal: Kuang departed; Zao lost the hearts of officers and men, and the city fell again.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang left, Zao lost the troops' loyalty and the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 給事中熊汝霖、御史遊有倫劾曠沔陽失城罪，候訊黃州。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xiong Rulin and the censor You Youlun impeached Kuang for the crime of losing Mianyang and he awaited interrogation at Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xiong Rulin and Censor You Youlun impeached him for losing Mianyang, and he awaited trial at Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 用騰蛟薦，令戴罪立功。

translations.literal: On Tengjiao's recommendation he was ordered to redeem his guilt by achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: On Tengjiao's recommendation he was allowed to redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 福王立南京，左良玉將犯闕。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing; Zuo Liangyu was about to march on the capital in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, Zuo Liangyu was preparing to march on the capital in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟至長沙，以曠為監軍。

translations.literal: When Tengjiao reached Changsha he made Kuang army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Tengjiao reached Changsha he made Kuang his army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 副將黃朝宣者，故巡撫宋一鶴部將，駐燕子窩，騰蛟令曠召之來。

translations.literal: The deputy general Huang Chaoxuan had been a subordinate of the former grand coordinator Song Yihe and was stationed at Yanziwuo; Tengjiao ordered Kuang to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Huang Chaoxuan, formerly under Grand Coordinator Song Yihe, was at Yanziwuo; Tengjiao had Kuang summon him.

sentences.zh: 副將張先璧屯精騎三千於漵浦，復屬曠召之，留為親軍，而以朝宣戍茶陵。

translations.literal: Deputy General Zhang Xianbi encamped three thousand elite cavalry at Xupu; Kuang was again charged to summon him, kept him as personal troops, and posted Chaoxuan to garrison Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy General Zhang Xianbi held three thousand elite cavalry at Xupu; Kuang summoned him as well, kept him as a personal guard, and posted Chaoxuan at Chaling.

sentences.zh: 又令曠調劉承胤兵於武岡。

translations.literal: He also ordered Kuang to summon Liu Chengyin's troops at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Kuang rally Liu Chengyin's troops at Wugang.

sentences.zh: 會李自成死，其下劉體仁、郝搖旗、袁宗第、藺養成、王進才、牛有勇六大部各擁數萬兵至。

translations.literal: Just then Li Zicheng died; beneath him Liu Tiren, Hao Yaoqi, Yuan Zongdi, Lan Yangcheng, Wang Jincai, and Niu Youyong—the six great divisions—each leading tens of thousands of troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had just died; his six great divisions under Liu Tiren, Hao Yaoqi, Yuan Zongdi, Lan Yangcheng, Wang Jincai, and Niu Youyong arrived, each with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟與曠計，盡撫其眾，軍容大壯。

translations.literal: Tengjiao and Kuang devised a plan and pacified all their hosts; military strength grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao and Kuang worked out a plan to win them all over, and the army's strength swelled dramatically.

sentences.zh: 左良玉死，其將馬進忠、王允成無所歸，突至岳州。

translations.literal: When Zuo Liangyu died his generals Ma Jinzhong and Wang Yuncheng, with nowhere to go, suddenly appeared at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo Liangyu's death his generals Ma Jinzhong and Wang Yuncheng, leaderless, suddenly appeared at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 偏沅巡撫傅上瑞大懼，曠曰：「此無主之兵，可撫也。」

translations.literal: The western Hunan grand coordinator Fu Shangrui was greatly afraid; Kuang said: "These are troops without a master—they can be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Western Hunan Grand Coordinator Fu Shangrui was terrified; Kuang said, "These are leaderless troops—they can be won over."

sentences.zh: 入其營，與進忠握手，指白水為誓，進忠等皆從之。

translations.literal: He entered their camp, clasped hands with Jinzhong, and pointed to the white water as oath; Jinzhong and the others all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered their camp, clasped Jinzhong's hand, and swore an oath over clear water; Jinzhong and the rest submitted.

sentences.zh: 進忠即賊中渠魁混十萬也。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was none other than Hun Shiwan, a chieftain among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was none other than Hun Shiwan, a chief among the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時南京已破，大兵逼湖南，諸將皆畏怯，曠獨悉力禦。

translations.literal: By then Nanjing had fallen and the great army pressed Hunan; the generals were all fearful and timid, but Kuang alone exerted his full strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had fallen and the Qing armies pressed Hunan; the other generals quailed, but Kuang alone fought with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 唐王擢為右僉都御史，提督軍務，恢剿湖北。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince promoted him to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, charged him to supervise military affairs, and recover and pacify Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince promoted him to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, put him in charge of military affairs, and charged him with recovering Hubei.

sentences.zh: 曠有智略，行軍不避鋒鏑。

translations.literal: Kuang had strategic talent and in campaigning did not shun the clash of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was resourceful and never shrank from the front line.

sentences.zh: 身扼湘陰、平江之沖，湖南恃以無恐。

translations.literal: He personally held the strategic passes of Xiangyin and Pingjiang; Hunan relied on him and was without fear.
translations.idiomatic: He personally held the strategic junction of Xiangyin and Pingjiang, and Hunan rested secure behind him.

sentences.zh: 嘗戰岳州，以後軍不繼而還。

translations.literal: He once fought at Yuezhou but withdrew because the rear army did not follow up.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Yuezhou once but withdrew when his rear failed to support him.

sentences.zh: 已，又大戰大荊驛。

translations.literal: Later he fought another great battle at Dajing Post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fought another major engagement at Dajing Post.

sentences.zh: 永明王加兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The Yongli Prince added the title Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongli Emperor promoted him to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 長沙守將王進才與狼兵將覃遇春哄，大掠而去。

translations.literal: The Changsha garrison commander Wang Jincai quarreled with the Lang soldier general Qin Yuchun and after great pillaging departed.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha garrison commander Wang Jincai quarreled with the Lang general Qin Yuchun, plundered the city, and marched away.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟奔衡州，曠亦走寶慶，長沙遂失。

translations.literal: Tengjiao fled to Hengzhou; Kuang also fled to Baoqing, and Changsha was then lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao fled to Hengzhou; Kuang withdrew to Baoqing, and Changsha fell.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟駐祁陽，曠來會。

translations.literal: Tengjiao was stationed at Qiyang; Kuang came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao was at Qiyang when Kuang came to join him.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟以兵事屬曠，而謁王武岡。

translations.literal: Tengjiao entrusted military affairs to Kuang and himself went to pay court to the prince at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao left military affairs to Kuang and went to court at Wugang.

sentences.zh: 曠移駐永州，見諸大將擁兵，聞警輒走，抑郁而卒。

translations.literal: Kuang shifted his station to Yongzhou; seeing the great generals hugging their troops and fleeing at every alarm, he sank into depression and died.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang moved to Yongzhou; watching the great generals clutch their private armies and flee at every alarm, he sank into despair and died.

sentences.zh: 傅作霖，武陵人。

translations.literal: Fu Zuolin was a native of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuolin came from Wuling.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉仕唐王，大學士蘇觀生奏為職方主事，監紀其軍。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he entered the service of the Tang Prince; Grand Secretary Su Guansheng memorialized to make him a director in the Bureau of Appointments to supervise the prince's army.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial examination he entered the Tang Prince's service; Grand Secretary Su Guansheng had him appointed Bureau of Appointments director to supervise the prince's army.

sentences.zh: 觀生歿，倚何騰蛟長沙，改監軍御史。

translations.literal: When Guansheng died he relied on He Tengjiao at Changsha and was changed to army-supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: After Guansheng's death he attached himself to He Tengjiao at Changsha and became army-supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 永明王在全州，超拜兵部左侍郎，掌部事，尋進尚書，從至武岡。

translations.literal: When the Yongli Prince was at Quanzhou he was promoted over the regular ranks to Left Vice Minister of War and directed the ministry; shortly he was advanced to minister and followed the court to Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: While the Yongli Emperor was at Quanzhou he was rapidly promoted to Left Vice Minister of War and put in charge of the ministry, soon advanced to full minister, and followed the court to Wugang.

sentences.zh: 時劉承胤擅政，作霖與相善，故驟遷。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Chengyin monopolized government; Zuolin was on good terms with him and therefore rose rapidly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengyin then dominated the government; Zuolin was his ally and rose swiftly.

sentences.zh: 及大兵逼武岡，承胤議迎降，作霖勃然責之。

translations.literal: When the great army pressed Wugang, Chengyin proposed welcoming surrender; Zuolin rebuked him in a fury.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing armies closed on Wugang, Chengyin proposed surrender; Zuolin rebuked him hotly.

sentences.zh: 承胤遣使納款，大兵入城，作霖冠帶坐堂上。

translations.literal: Chengyin sent envoys to offer submission; the great army entered the city; Zuolin sat in full cap and belt in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin sent envoys to submit; as the Qing troops entered the city, Zuolin sat in full court dress in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 承胤力勸之降，不從，遂被殺。

translations.literal: Chengyin urged him strongly to surrender; he would not agree and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyin pressed him to surrender; he refused and was executed.

sentences.zh: 妾鄭有殊色，被執，驅之過橋，躍入水中死。

translations.literal: His concubine Zheng was of unusual beauty; seized and driven across a bridge, she leaped into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Zheng, a woman of striking beauty, was seized and driven across a bridge; she leaped into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 有蕭曠者，武昌諸生，為承胤坐營參將。

translations.literal: There was one Xiao Kuang, a licentiate of Wuchang, who served as Chengyin's camp deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xiao Kuang, a Wuchang licentiate who served as Chengyin's camp deputy general.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟題為總兵官，管黎平參將事。

translations.literal: Tengjiao nominated him as regional commander-in-chief in charge of the Liping deputy general's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao appointed him regional commander with charge of the Liping deputy general's command.

sentences.zh: 及承胤降，令降將陳友龍招曠，曠不從。

translations.literal: When Chengyin surrendered, he ordered the surrendered general Chen Youlong to summon Kuang; Kuang would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengyin surrendered, he sent the defector Chen Youlong to win Kuang over; Kuang refused.

sentences.zh: 已而城破，死之。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell and he died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell, and he died defending it.

sentences.zh: 傅上瑞，初為武昌推官，賊圍城，遁走。

translations.literal: Fu Shangrui had first been magistrate-adjunct of Wuchang; when bandits besieged the city he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shangrui had been magistrate-adjunct of Wuchang; when rebels besieged the city he fled.

sentences.zh: 久之，騰蛟薦為長沙僉事，又令攝偏沅巡撫事。

translations.literal: After a long while Tengjiao recommended him as Changsha intendant and also ordered him to act as western Hunan grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tengjiao recommended him as Changsha intendant and put him in charge of western Hunan as acting grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 勸騰蛟設十三鎮，卒為湖南大害。

translations.literal: He urged Tengjiao to establish the Thirteen Garrisons, which in the end became a great calamity for Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Tengjiao to establish the Thirteen Garrisons, which ultimately became Hunan's greatest scourge.

sentences.zh: 唐王時，用騰蛟薦，擢右僉都御史，實授偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the Tang Prince's time, on Tengjiao's recommendation he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and formally appointed western Hunan grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang Prince, on Tengjiao's recommendation he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and confirmed as grand coordinator of western Hunan.

sentences.zh: 性反覆，棄騰蛟如遺。

translations.literal: His nature was fickle; he cast off Tengjiao as if discarding something left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Fickle by nature, he cast Tengjiao aside without a thought.

sentences.zh: 武岡破，大兵逼沅州，上瑞出降。

translations.literal: When Wugang fell and the great army pressed Yuanzhou, Shangrui came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Wugang fell and the Qing armies closed on Yuanzhou, Shangrui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 逾年，與劉承胤並誅死。

translations.literal: More than a year later he was executed together with Liu Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was executed along with Liu Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 瞿式耜，字起田，常熟人。

translations.literal: Qu Shisi, courtesy name Qitian, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Shisi, courtesy name Qitian, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎景淳孫，湖廣參議汝說子也。

translations.literal: He was grandson of Vice Minister of Rites Qu Jingchun and son of Huguang Administrative Commissioner Qu Yueshuo.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Vice Minister of Rites Qu Jingchun and the son of Huguang Administrative Commissioner Qu Yueshuo.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授吉安永豐知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Ji'an and governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Yongfeng in Ji'an, he won the people with humane government.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年調江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was transferred to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he was transferred to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 永豐民乞留，命再任。

translations.literal: The people of Yongfeng begged that he remain, and he was ordered to serve a second term.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yongfeng petitioned to keep him, and he was ordered to serve another term.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，擢戶科給事中，疏言李國𣚴宜留內閣，王永光宜典銓，曹於汴宜秉憲，鄭三俊、畢懋良宜總版曹，李邦華宜主戎政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was promoted to supervising secretary in the revenue section and memorialized that Li Guozhuang ought to remain in the Grand Secretariat, Wang Yongguang ought to oversee appointments, Cao Yubian ought to hold the law, Zheng Sanjun and Bi Maoliang ought to direct the Ministry of Works, and Li Banghua ought to direct military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was made supervising secretary in the revenue section and urged that Li Guozhuang stay in the Grand Secretariat, Wang Yongguang head appointments, Cao Yubian take charge of law, Zheng Sanjun and Bi Maoliang run the Ministry of Works, and Li Banghua direct military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝多采其言。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted much of what he said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted most of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 俄陳朝政不平，為王之寀請恤，孫慎行訟冤，速楊鎬、王化貞之誅，白楊漣、左光鬥結毒之謗，追論故相魏廣微、顧秉謙、馮銓、黃立極之罪。

translations.literal: Shortly he set forth the injustices of court government, sought posthumous favor for Wang Zhicai, pleaded the wrong done to Sun Shenxing, urged swift execution of Yang Hao and Wang Huazhen, cleared the poisoned slanders against Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou, and pursued judgment on the former chancellors Wei Guangwei, Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, and Huang Liji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he exposed court injustices, sought honors for Wang Zhicai, vindicated Sun Shenxing, demanded the punishment of Yang Hao and Wang Huazhen, cleared the slanders against Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou, and pressed charges against the former chancellors Wei Guangwei, Gu Bingqian, Feng Quan, and Huang Liji.

sentences.zh: 因言奪情建祠之朱童蒙不可寬，積愆久廢之湯賓尹不可用。

translations.literal: He also said that Zhu Tongmeng, who had left mourning to build a shrine, could not be pardoned, and that Tang Binyin, long disgraced for accumulated faults, could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Zhu Tongmeng, who had left mourning early to erect a shrine, must not be pardoned, and that Tang Binyin, long disgraced for repeated offenses, must not be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝亦納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted these points as well.

sentences.zh: 又極論來宗道、楊景辰附逆不可居政府，二人旋罷去。

translations.literal: He also argued forcefully that Lai Zongdao and Yang Jingchen, who had joined the rebels, could not remain in government, and the two were soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He also insisted that Lai Zongdao and Yang Jingchen, having sided with the rebels, could not hold office, and both were soon removed.

sentences.zh: 御史袁弘勛劾大學士劉鴻訓，逆黨徐大化實主之。

translations.literal: The censor Yuan Hongxun impeached Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun, but the eunuch faction member Xu Dahua was the real instigator.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Hongxun impeached Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun, though the eunuch partisan Xu Dahua was the real instigator.

sentences.zh: 川貴總督張鶴鳴先已被廢，其復用由魏忠賢。

translations.literal: Sichuan-Guizhou Supreme Commander Zhang Heming had earlier been dismissed; his restoration came through Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan-Guizhou Supreme Commander Zhang Heming had already been dismissed once; his restoration came through Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 式耜並疏論。

translations.literal: Shisi also memorialized on these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi memorialized on these matters as well.

sentences.zh: 已，頌楊漣、魏大中、周順昌為清中之清，忠中之忠，三人遂賜謚。

translations.literal: Later he praised Yang Lian, Wei Dazhong, and Zhou Shunchang as the purest among the pure and the loyal among the loyal, and the three were granted posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Later he praised Yang Lian, Wei Dazhong, and Zhou Shunchang as the purest of the pure and the loyal among the loyal, and all three received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 未幾，陳時務七事，言：「起廢不可不核，升遷不可不漸，會推不可不慎。

translations.literal: Before long he set forth seven items of current policy, saying: "Restoring the dismissed must be scrutinized, promotions must be gradual, and joint recommendation must be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he presented seven policy recommendations: "Reinstatements must be carefully vetted, promotions must be gradual, and joint nominations must be made with caution.

sentences.zh: 謚典宜嚴，刑章宜飭，論人宜審，附珰者宜區分。」

translations.literal: Posthumous honors ought to be strict, penal codes ought to be tightened, judging men ought to be careful, and those who attached to the eunuchs ought to be distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors should be strict, penal law should be enforced, judgments of character should be careful, and eunuch allies should be clearly distinguished."

sentences.zh: 又極論館選奔競之弊，請臨軒親試。

translations.literal: He also argued forcefully against the abuses of scrambling in Hanlin selection and asked that the emperor personally examine candidates at court.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced the corruption of Hanlin selection and asked the emperor to examine candidates in person at court.

sentences.zh: 末言：「古有左右史，記天子言動。

translations.literal: At the end he said: "In antiquity there were the left and right historiographers who recorded the Son of Heaven's words and actions.
translations.idiomatic: Finally he said, "In antiquity the left and right historiographers recorded the emperor's words and deeds.

sentences.zh: 今召對時勤，宜令史官入侍紀錄，昭示朝野。」

translations.literal: Now that imperial audiences are frequent, historiographers ought to enter attendance and record them, making this known within and without the court."
translations.idiomatic: Now that audiences are frequent, historiographers should attend and record them for all court and country to see."

sentences.zh: 事多議行。

translations.literal: Many of these proposals were debated and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Many of these proposals were adopted after debate.

sentences.zh: 時將定逆案，請盡發紅本，定其情罪輕重。

translations.literal: As the treason cases were about to be settled, he asked that all the vermilion memorials be fully released to fix the gravity of each man's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: As the treason cases were being settled, he asked that all vermilion memorials be published so each man's guilt could be weighed.

sentences.zh: 又言宣府巡撫徐良彥不附逆奄，為崔呈秀誣劾遣戍，亟當登用。

translations.literal: He also said that Xuanfu Grand Coordinator Xu Liangyan had not joined the rebel eunuchs, was falsely impeached by Cui Chengxi and sent into exile, and ought urgently to be reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Xuanfu Grand Coordinator Xu Liangyan, who had refused the eunuch faction, was falsely impeached by Cui Chengxi and exiled, and should be restored at once.

sentences.zh: 良彥遂獲起。

translations.literal: Liangyan was then restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyan was duly restored.

sentences.zh: 式耜矯矯立名，所建白多當帝意，然搏擊權豪，大臣多畏其口。

translations.literal: Shisi stood aloof in establishing his reputation; most of what he proposed suited the emperor's mind, yet he struck at the powerful and great, and many ministers feared his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi built a reputation for uncompromising integrity; most of his proposals pleased the emperor, but he attacked the powerful, and many ministers feared his tongue.

sentences.zh: 十月詔會推閣臣，禮部侍郎錢謙益以同官周延儒方言事蒙眷，慮並推則己絀，謀沮之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered joint recommendation of Grand Secretaries; Vice Minister of Rites Qian Qianyi, because his colleague Zhou Yanru had won favor by reporting local dialect affairs, feared that if both were recommended he would be outshone and plotted to block it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court ordered joint nomination of Grand Secretaries; Vice Minister of Rites Qian Qianyi, seeing his colleague Zhou Yanru favored for reporting on regional affairs, feared being outranked if both were nominated and plotted to block Zhou.

sentences.zh: 式耜，謙益門人也，言於當事者，擯延儒弗推，而列謙益第二。

translations.literal: Shisi was Qianyi's student; he spoke to those in charge to exclude Yanru from recommendation and rank Qianyi second.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi, Qianyi's student, persuaded those in charge to exclude Yanru and rank Qianyi second.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁遂發難，延儒助之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren then raised objections, and Yanru assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren then attacked the nomination, with Yanru's support.

sentences.zh: 謙益奪官閑住，式耜坐貶謫。

translations.literal: Qianyi was stripped of office and left idle; Shisi was demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was stripped of office and sent home; Shisi was demoted and exiled.

sentences.zh: 式耜嘗頌貴寧參政胡平表殺賊功，請優擢。

translations.literal: Shisi had once praised Guining Administrative Commissioner Hu Pingbiao for merit in killing bandits and asked that he be specially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi had once praised Guining Commissioner Hu Pingbiao for defeating bandits and asked that he be specially promoted.

sentences.zh: 其後平表為貴州布政使，坐不謹罷。

translations.literal: Later Pingbiao became Guizhou administrative commissioner and was dismissed for lack of prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pingbiao became Guizhou administrative commissioner and was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 式耜再貶二秩，遂廢於家。

translations.literal: Shisi was demoted two more ranks and was then left idle at home.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi was demoted two more ranks and retired to private life.

sentences.zh: 久之，常熟奸民張漢儒希體仁指，訐謙益、式耜貪肆不法。

translations.literal: After a long while the Changshu scoundrel Zhang Hanru, hoping to please Tiren, denounced Qianyi and Shisi for greed and lawless conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the Changshu troublemaker Zhang Hanru, seeking Wen Tiren's favor, accused Qianyi and Shisi of corruption and lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 體仁主之，下法司逮治。

translations.literal: Tiren backed the accusation and handed them to the judicial offices for arrest and trial.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren backed the charges and had them arrested for trial.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張國維、巡按路振飛交章白其冤，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei and Touring Censor Lu Zhenfei submitted successive memorials declaring their innocence, but the court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei and Touring Censor Lu Zhenfei repeatedly declared their innocence, but the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 比兩人就獄，則體仁已去位，獄稍解。

translations.literal: By the time the two entered prison Tiren had already left office, and the case eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached prison Tiren had fallen from power, and the case eased.

sentences.zh: 謙益坐削籍，式耜贖徒。

translations.literal: Qianyi was struck from the rolls; Shisi was ransomed as a convict laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was struck from the rolls; Shisi paid a fine and was released.

sentences.zh: 言官疏薦，不納。

translations.literal: Censorial officials memorialized recommending him, but the recommendation was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censors recommended his restoration, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 十七年，福王立於南京。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 八月起式耜應天府丞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Shisi was recalled as vice prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
