translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shisi was recalled as vice prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 已，擢右僉都御史，代方震孺巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and replaced Fang Zhenru as Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Guangxi, replacing Fang Zhenru.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，甫抵梧州，聞南京破。

translations.literal: The next summer, having just reached Wuzhou, he heard that Nanjing had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, just as he reached Wuzhou, word came that Nanjing had fallen.

sentences.zh: 靖江王亨嘉謀僭號，召式耜。

translations.literal: The Jingjiang Prince Zhu Hengjia plotted to usurp the imperial title and summoned Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjiang Prince Zhu Hengjia plotted to declare himself emperor and summoned Shisi.

sentences.zh: 拒不往，而檄思恩參將陳邦傳助防。

translations.literal: Shisi refused to go and instead issued orders to the Si'en Deputy General Chen Bangchuan to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi refused and instead ordered Si'en Deputy General Chen Bangchuan to help defend the province.

sentences.zh: 止狼兵，勿應亨嘉調。

translations.literal: He halted the Lang troops and forbade them to answer Hengjia's summons.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Lang troops back and forbade them to obey Hengjia's orders.

sentences.zh: 亨嘉至梧，劫式耜，幽之桂林，遣入取其敕印。

translations.literal: Hengjia reached Wuzhou, seized Shisi, imprisoned him at Guilin, and sent men in to take his commission and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Hengjia reached Wuzhou, seized Shisi, imprisoned him at Guilin, and sent men to take his commission and seal.

sentences.zh: 初，式耜議立桂端王子安仁王。

translations.literal: Earlier Shisi had proposed enthroning the Prince of Anren, son of the Gui Prince Zhu Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shisi had favored enthroning the Prince of Anren, son of the Gui Prince Zhu Duan.

sentences.zh: 及唐王監國，式耜以為倫序不當立，不奉表勸進。

translations.literal: When the Tang Prince became regent, Shisi held that the order of succession made his enthronement improper and did not submit a memorial urging him to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang Prince became regent, Shisi held that succession rules made his claim improper and refused to submit a memorial urging his enthronement.

sentences.zh: 至是為亨嘉所幽，乃遣使賀王，因乞援。

translations.literal: Now, imprisoned by Hengjia, he sent envoys to congratulate the prince and thereby beg for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Now imprisoned by Hengjia, he sent envoys to congratulate the Tang Prince and beg for rescue.

sentences.zh: 王喜，而亨嘉為丁魁楚所攻，勢窘，乃釋式耜。

translations.literal: The prince was pleased, but Hengjia, attacked by Ding Kuitu, was in dire straits and then released Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was pleased; Hengjia, pressed by Ding Kuitu, grew desperate and released Shisi.

sentences.zh: 式耜與中軍官焦璉召邦傳共執亨嘉，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Shisi and the central army officer Jiao Lian summoned Bangchuan to seize Hengjia together, and the turmoil was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi and central army officer Jiao Lian joined Bangchuan in seizing Hengjia, and the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 唐王擢式耜兵部右侍郎，協理戎政，以晏日曙來代。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince promoted Shisi to Right Vice Minister of War to assist in military affairs, with Yan Rishu coming to replace him as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince made him Right Vice Minister of War with charge of military affairs, and Yan Rishu replaced him as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 式耜不入朝，退居廣東。

translations.literal: Shisi did not enter court but withdrew to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi did not go to court but withdrew to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 順治三年九月，大兵破汀州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Shunzhi the great army took Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year of Shunzhi the Qing armies took Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 式耜與魁楚等議立永明王由榔，乃迎王梧州，以十月十日監國肇慶。

translations.literal: Shisi with Kuitu and others deliberated enthroning the Yongli Prince Zhu Youlang; they welcomed the prince to Wuzhou and on the tenth day of the tenth month installed him as regent at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi and Kuitu and others resolved to enthrone the Yongli Prince Zhu Youlang; they brought him to Wuzhou and on the tenth day of the tenth month installed him as regent at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 進式耜吏部右侍郎、東閣大學士，兼掌吏部事。

translations.literal: Shisi was advanced to Right Vice Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, concurrently directing the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi was made Right Vice Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，贛州敗報至，司禮王坤迫王赴梧州。

translations.literal: Before long news arrived of defeat at Ganzhou; the Director of Ceremonies Wang Kun pressed the prince to go to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon news of defeat at Ganzhou arrived; Director of Ceremonies Wang Kun pressed the emperor to flee to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 式耜力爭，不得。

translations.literal: Shisi argued forcefully but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi argued fiercely but could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 十一月朔，蘇觀生立唐王聿𨮁於廣州。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month Su Guansheng enthroned the Tang Prince Zhu Yuyue at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month Su Guansheng proclaimed Zhu Yuyue emperor at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 式耜乃與魁楚等定議迎王還肇慶，遣總督林佳鼎禦觀生兵，敗歿。

translations.literal: Shisi then with Kuitu and others resolved to welcome the prince back to Zhaoqing and sent Supreme Commander Lin Jiading to resist Guansheng's army; he was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi and Kuitu then resolved to bring the emperor back to Zhaoqing and sent Supreme Commander Lin Jiading against Guansheng's forces; Lin was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 式耜視師峽口。

translations.literal: Shisi personally directed the army at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi took command in person at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 十二月望，大兵破廣州。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the twelfth month the great army took Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the twelfth month the Qing armies took Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王坤趣王西走。

translations.literal: Wang Kun urged the prince to flee westward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun urged the emperor to flee westward.

sentences.zh: 式耜趨赴王，王已越梧而西。

translations.literal: Shisi hurried to join the prince, but the prince had already passed west beyond Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi hurried after the emperor, but he had already fled west beyond Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，大兵破肇慶，逼梧州，巡撫曹曄迎降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the great army took Zhaoqing and pressed Wuzhou; Grand Coordinator Cao Ye came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Qing took Zhaoqing and closed on Wuzhou; Grand Coordinator Cao Ye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王欲走依何騰蛟於湖廣，丁魁楚、呂大器、王化澄皆棄王去，止式耜及吳炳、吳貞毓等從，乃由平樂抵桂林。

translations.literal: The prince wished to flee to rely on He Tengjiao in Huguang; Ding Kuitu, Lü Daqi, and Wang Huacheng all abandoned the prince and left; only Shisi and Wu Bing, Wu Zhenyu, and others followed, and they went by Pingle to reach Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to seek refuge with He Tengjiao in Huguang; Ding Kuitu, Lü Daqi, and Wang Huacheng all deserted him; only Shisi, Wu Bing, Wu Zhenyu, and a few others remained, and they reached Guilin by way of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 二月，大兵襲平樂，分兵趨桂林。

translations.literal: In the second month the great army struck Pingle and sent detachments toward Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Qing struck Pingle and sent columns toward Guilin.

sentences.zh: 王將走全州，式耜極陳桂林形勢，請留，不許。

translations.literal: The prince was about to flee to Quanzhou; Shisi set forth the strategic situation of Guilin at length and begged him to remain, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prepared to flee to Quanzhou; Shisi argued at length for holding Guilin, but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 自請留守，許之。

translations.literal: He asked to remain behind as garrison commander and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to stay and hold the city, and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 進文淵閣大學士，兼兵部尚書，賜劍，便宜從事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness, concurrently Minister of War, granted the sword, and authorized to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Deepness and Minister of War, granted the imperial sword, and authorized to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 平樂、潯州相繼破，桂林危甚。

translations.literal: Pingle and Xunzhou fell in succession; Guilin was in extreme peril.
translations.idiomatic: Pingle and Xunzhou fell in turn, and Guilin was in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 總督侍郎朱盛濃走靈川，巡按御史辜延泰走融縣，布政使朱盛氵調、副使楊垂雲、桂林知府王惠卿以下皆遁，惟式耜與通判鄭國藩，縣丞李世榮及都司林應昌、李當瑞、沈煌在焉。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Vice Minister Zhu Shengnong fled to Lingchuan; Touring Censor Gu Yantai fled to Rong County; Administrative Commissioner Zhu Shengdiao, Vice Commissioner Yang Chuiyun, Guilin Prefect Wang Huiqing, and all below them fled; only Shisi, Magistrate-Adjunct Zheng Guofan, Assistant Magistrate Li Shirong, and Regional Commanders Lin Yingchang, Li Dangrui, and Shen Huang remained.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Zhu Shengnong fled to Lingchuan; Touring Censor Gu Yantai fled to Rong County; Administrative Commissioner Zhu Shengdiao, Vice Commissioner Yang Chuiyun, Prefect Wang Huiqing, and the rest all fled; only Shisi, Adjunct Magistrate Zheng Guofan, Assistant Magistrate Li Shirong, and Regional Commanders Lin Yingchang, Li Dangrui, and Shen Huang stayed.

sentences.zh: 王令兵部右侍郎丁元曄代盛濃，御史魯可藻代延泰。

translations.literal: The prince ordered Right Vice Minister of War Ding Yuanye to replace Shengnong and Censor Lu Kezao to replace Yantai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Right Vice Minister Ding Yuanye to replace Zhu Shengnong and Censor Lu Kezao to replace Gu Yantai.

sentences.zh: 未赴而大兵已於三月薄桂林，以騎數十突入文昌門，登城樓瞰式耜公署。

translations.literal: Before they arrived the great army in the third month had already pressed Guilin; several dozen horsemen burst through the Wenchang Gate, climbed the gate tower, and looked down on Shisi's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could take up their posts, in the third month the Qing closed on Guilin; dozens of horsemen burst through the Wenchang Gate, mounted the tower, and looked down on Shisi's compound.

sentences.zh: 式耜急令援將焦璉拒戰。

translations.literal: Shisi urgently ordered the relief general Jiao Lian to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi urgently ordered relief general Jiao Lian into the fight.

sentences.zh: 初，永明王為賊執，璉率眾攀城上，破械出之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Yongli Prince had been seized by bandits, Lian led his men scaling the city wall and broke his bonds to bring him out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when bandits had seized the Yongli Prince, Lian scaled the walls with his men and broke him free.

sentences.zh: 王病不能行，璉負王以行。

translations.literal: The prince was ill and could not walk; Lian carried the prince on his back as they went.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was too ill to walk; Lian carried him on his back.

sentences.zh: 王以此德璉，用破靖江王功，命為參將。

translations.literal: The prince for this reason was grateful to Lian; on the merit of defeating the Jingjiang Prince he was appointed deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for this, the prince rewarded him for crushing the Jingjiang rebellion by making him a deputy general.

sentences.zh: 及是戰守三月，璉功最多，元曄、可藻亦盡力。

translations.literal: In this fighting and defense of three months Lian's merit was greatest; Yuanye and Kezao also exerted their full strength.
translations.idiomatic: In three months of fighting Lian's merit was greatest; Yuanye and Kezao also gave their all.

sentences.zh: 式耜身立矢石中，與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Shisi himself stood amid arrows and stones, sharing hardship and comfort with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi stood in the line of fire himself, sharing hardship with his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 積雨城壞，吏士無人色，式耜督城守自如，故人無叛誌。

translations.literal: Prolonged rain ruined the walls; officials and soldiers lost all color in their faces, yet Shisi directed the defense as calmly as ever, so that no one harbored thoughts of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Weeks of rain breached the walls; officials and soldiers turned pale, yet Shisi directed the defense unshaken, and no one thought of treason.

sentences.zh: 援兵索餉而嘩，式耜括庫不足，妻邵捐簪珥佐之。

translations.literal: Relief troops demanded pay and clamored; Shisi emptied the treasury but it was not enough, and his wife Lady Shao donated her hairpins and earrings to help.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops clamored for pay; the treasury could not cover it, and his wife Lady Shao gave her jewelry to help.

sentences.zh: 既而璉兵主客不和，噪而去，城幾破者數矣。

translations.literal: Before long Lian's troops, host and guest ill at ease, clamored and departed; several times the city was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lian's troops, alienated from the garrison, mutinied and left; the city nearly fell several times.

sentences.zh: 會陳邦彥等攻廣州，大兵引而東，桂林獲全。

translations.literal: Just then Chen Bangyan and others attacked Guangzhou; the great army drew off eastward and Guilin was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Chen Bangyan attacked Guangzhou; the Qing armies turned east, and Guilin was saved.

sentences.zh: 璉亦復陽朔及平樂，陳邦傳亦由潯復梧州。

translations.literal: Lian also recovered Yangshuo and Pingle, and Chen Bangchuan from Xun recovered Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lian retook Yangshuo and Pingle, and Chen Bangchuan retook Wuzhou from Xun.

sentences.zh: 王聞捷，封式耜臨桂伯，璉新興伯，元曄等進秩有差。

translations.literal: When the prince heard of the victory he enfeoffed Shisi as Earl of Lingui, Lian as Earl of Xinxing, and advanced Yuanye and the others in rank to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the victory, the emperor enfeoffed Shisi as Earl of Lingui and Lian as Earl of Xinxing, and promoted Yuanye and the others.

sentences.zh: 式耜初請王返全州，不聽。

translations.literal: Shisi at first asked the prince to return to Quanzhou, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi had first urged the emperor to return to Quanzhou, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 已，請還桂林。

translations.literal: Later he asked to return to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to return to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 王已許之，會武岡破，王由靖州走柳州，式耜復請還桂林。

translations.literal: The prince had already agreed, but when Wugang fell the prince fled from Jingzhou to Liuzhou, and Shisi again asked to return to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had agreed, but when Wugang fell he fled from Jingzhou to Liuzhou, and Shisi again urged a return to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大兵自湖南逼全州，式耜偕騰蛟拒卻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the great army pressed Quanzhou from Hunan; Shisi together with Tengjiao repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Qing advanced on Quanzhou from Hunan; Shisi and Tengjiao drove them back.

sentences.zh: 已，梧州復破，王方在象州，欲走南寧。

translations.literal: Before long Wuzhou fell again; the prince was then at Xiangzhou and wished to flee to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wuzhou fell again; the emperor was at Xiangzhou and prepared to flee to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 以大臣力爭，乃以十二月還桂林。

translations.literal: Because the ministers argued forcefully, in the twelfth month he returned to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers argued him back, and in the twelfth month he returned to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，南安侯郝永忠駐桂林，惡城外團練兵，盡破水東十八村，殺戮無算，與式耜構難。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year the Nan'an Marquis Hao Yongzhong was stationed at Guilin; he hated the militia outside the walls, utterly destroyed the eighteen villages east of the river, slaughtered beyond counting, and came into conflict with Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year Nan'an Marquis Hao Yongzhong was at Guilin; he hated the suburban militia, destroyed the eighteen villages east of the river, massacred without limit, and clashed with Shisi.

sentences.zh: 式耜力調劑，永忠乃駐興安。

translations.literal: Shisi mediated with all his strength, and Yongzhong then garrisoned Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi mediated strenuously, and Yongzhong withdrew to Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 大兵前驅至靈川，永忠戰敗，奔入桂林，請王即夕西走。

translations.literal: The vanguard of the great army reached Lingchuan; Yongzhong was defeated in battle, fled into Guilin, and asked the prince to flee west that very night.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing vanguard reached Lingchuan; Yongzhong was beaten and fled into Guilin, urging the emperor to flee west that night.

sentences.zh: 式耜力爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Shisi argued forcefully but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi protested fiercely but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 左右皆請速駕，式耜又爭。

translations.literal: Those at the prince's side all urged a swift departure; Shisi argued again.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers all urged immediate flight; Shisi argued again.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「卿不過欲予死社稷爾。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "You only wish me to die for the altars of state and land."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You only want me to die for the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 式耜為泣下沾衣。

translations.literal: Shisi wept until his tears soaked his robes.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi wept until his robes were soaked with tears.

sentences.zh: 王甫行，永忠即大掠，捶殺太常卿黃太元。

translations.literal: The prince had barely departed when Yongzhong carried out great pillaging and beat to death the Minister of Ceremonies Huang Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had scarcely left when Yongzhong looted the city and beat Minister of Ceremonies Huang Taiyuan to death.

sentences.zh: 式耜家亦被掠，家人矯騰蛟令箭，乃出城。

translations.literal: Shisi's household was also plundered; his family members forged Tengjiao's command arrow and only then got out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi's household was looted as well; his family forged one of Tengjiao's command arrows and only then escaped the city.

sentences.zh: 日中，趙印選諸營自靈川至，亦大掠，城內外如洗。

translations.literal: At midday Zhao Yinxuan's camps arrived from Lingchuan and also carried out great pillaging; within and without the city was swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: At midday Zhao Yinxuan's troops arrived from Lingchuan and looted as well; the city was stripped bare inside and out.

sentences.zh: 永忠走柳州，印選等走永寧。

translations.literal: Yongzhong fled to Liuzhou; Yinxuan and the others fled to Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong fled to Liuzhou; Yinxuan and the rest fled to Yongning.

sentences.zh: 明日，式耜息城中余燼，安撫遠近。

translations.literal: The next day Shisi quelled the remaining fires in the city and comforted those near and far.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shisi put out the city's remaining fires and reassured the populace.

sentences.zh: 焦璉及諸鎮周金、湯兆佐、胡一青等各率所部至，騰蛟軍亦至。

translations.literal: Jiao Lian and the garrison commanders Zhou Jin, Tang Zhaozuo, Hu Yiqing, and others each led their units to arrive; Tengjiao's army also came.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lian and the garrison commanders Zhou Jin, Tang Zhaozuo, Hu Yiqing, and others marched in with their troops; Tengjiao's army arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 三月，大兵知桂林有變，來襲，抵北門。

translations.literal: In the third month the great army, learning of turmoil in Guilin, came to attack and reached the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, hearing of the turmoil in Guilin, the Qing attacked and reached the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 騰蛟督諸將拒戰，城獲全。

translations.literal: Tengjiao directed the generals in resisting battle, and the city was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Tengjiao directed the defense, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 時王駐南寧，式耜遣使慰三宮起居。

translations.literal: At the time the prince was stationed at Nanning; Shisi sent envoys to inquire after the health of the three palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Nanning; Shisi sent envoys to inquire after the imperial family's welfare.

sentences.zh: 王始知式耜無恙，為泣下。

translations.literal: The prince only then learned that Shisi was unharmed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Shisi was safe, the emperor wept.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，廣東李成棟、江西金聲桓皆叛大清，據地歸，式耜請王還桂林。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month Li Chengdong of Guangdong and Jin Shengheng of Jiangxi both rebelled against the Great Qing, held territory, and returned to allegiance; Shisi asked the prince to go back to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month Li Chengdong in Guangdong and Jin Shengheng in Jiangxi both rebelled against the Qing and submitted; Shisi urged the emperor to return to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 王從成棟請，將赴廣州。

translations.literal: The prince followed Chengdong's request and was about to go to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Chengdong's invitation and prepared to go to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 式耜慮成棟挾王自專，如劉承胤事，力爭之，乃駐肇慶。

translations.literal: Shisi feared Chengdong would seize the prince and act on his own authority, as in Liu Chengyin's affair, argued forcefully against it, and the court then remained at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Chengdong would dominate the emperor as Liu Chengyin had, Shisi protested fiercely, and the court stayed at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，永州、寶慶、衡州並復。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yongzhou, Baoqing, and Hengzhou were all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yongzhou, Baoqing, and Hengzhou were all retaken.

sentences.zh: 式耜以機會可乘，請王還桂林，圖出楚之計，不納。

translations.literal: Shisi, seeing the opportunity could be seized, asked the prince to return to Guilin and plan a strategy to break out into Chu; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a chance to strike, Shisi urged the emperor back to Guilin to plan a breakout into Hunan; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 慶國公陳邦傳守潯州，自稱世守廣西，欲如黔國公例。

translations.literal: The Qing State Duke Chen Bangchuan held Xunzhou, called himself hereditary guardian of Guangxi, and wished to follow the precedent of the Duke of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Qing State Duke Chen Bangchuan held Xunzhou, claimed hereditary rule over Guangxi, and sought status like the Duke of Qian.

sentences.zh: 式耜特疏劾之，會中外多爭者，邦傳乃止。

translations.literal: Shisi submitted a special memorial impeaching him; as many inside and outside court also disputed the claim, Bangchuan then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi memorialized against him; with widespread opposition at court, Bangchuan abandoned the claim.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫魯可藻自署銜巡撫兩廣，式耜亦疏駁之。

translations.literal: Guangxi Grand Coordinator Lu Kezao on his own authority styled himself Grand Coordinator of the Two Guangs; Shisi also memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Grand Coordinator Lu Kezao styled himself grand coordinator of both Guang provinces; Shisi memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 式耜身在外，政有闕，必疏諫。

translations.literal: Though Shisi was away from court, whenever government had faults he was sure to memorialize in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Though far from court, he memorialized whenever he saw a fault in policy.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「臣與主上患難相隨，休戚與共，不同他臣。

translations.literal: He once said: "Your servant and Your Majesty have shared hardship and follow each other in fortune and misfortune—not like other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Your servant has shared Your Majesty's hardships and fortunes—not like other ministers.

sentences.zh: 一切大政，自得與聞。」

translations.literal: All great affairs of state, I ought naturally to hear of them."
translations.idiomatic: I ought naturally to hear of every major decision."

sentences.zh: 王為褒納。

translations.literal: The prince praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 而是時成棟子元胤專朝政，知敬式耜，袁彭年、丁時魁、金堡等遂爭相倚附。

translations.literal: But by then Chengdong's son Yuan Yin monopolized court government, knew to respect Shisi, and Yuan Pengnian, Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and others vied to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chengdong's son Yuan Yin dominated the court, respected Shisi, and Yuan Pengnian, Ding Shikui, Jin Bao, and others competed to court him.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，時魁等逐朱天麟，不欲何吾騶為首輔。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Shikui and the others drove out Zhu Tianlin, not wishing He Wuzou to be chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Shikui and his faction expelled Zhu Tianlin to block He Wuzou from becoming chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 召式耜入直，以文淵印畀之，式耜終不入也。

translations.literal: They summoned Shisi to attend in the Secretariat and gave him the seal of the Hall of Literary Deepness, but Shisi in the end did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned him to the Secretariat and gave him the Hall of Literary Deepness seal, but Shisi never went.

sentences.zh: 未幾，騰蛟、聲桓、成棟相繼敗歿，國勢大危。

translations.literal: Before long Tengjiao, Shengheng, and Chengdong were defeated and killed in succession; the state's situation grew greatly perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tengjiao, Shengheng, and Chengdong fell in turn; the dynasty was in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 朝士方植黨相角，式耜不能禁。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen were just then forming factions and contending; Shisi could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Court factions were at each other's throats, and Shisi could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，南雄破。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Nanxiong fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Nanxiong fell.

sentences.zh: 王懼，走梧州。

translations.literal: The prince was afraid and fled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor fled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣訐時魁等下獄，式耜七疏論救。

translations.literal: The ministers impeached Shikui and the others and had them imprisoned; Shisi submitted seven memorials arguing for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers impeached Shikui and his faction and imprisoned them; Shisi submitted seven memorials in their defense.

sentences.zh: 胡執恭之擅封孫可望也，式耜疏請斬之。

translations.literal: When Hu Zhigong on his own authority enfeoffed Sun Kewang, Shisi memorialized asking that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Zhigong enfeoffed Sun Kewang on his own authority, Shisi memorialized demanding his execution.

sentences.zh: 皆不納。

translations.literal: None of these was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: None was heeded.

sentences.zh: 九月，全州破。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Quanzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Quanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 開國公趙印選居桂林，衛國公胡一青守榕江，與寧遠伯王永祚皆懼不出兵，大兵遂入嚴關。

translations.literal: The Founding State Duke Zhao Yinxuan was at Guilin, the Defender State Duke Hu Yiqing held Rongjiang, and together with the Pacifying Distance Earl Wang Yongzuo they were all afraid and would not march out; the great army then entered Yan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Founding State Duke Zhao Yinxuan held Guilin, Defender State Duke Hu Yiqing held Rongjiang, and Pacifying Distance Earl Wang Yongzuo—all too afraid to march out—so the Qing entered Yan Pass.

sentences.zh: 十月，一青、永祚入桂林分餉，榕江無戍兵，大兵益深入。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yiqing and Yongzuo entered Guilin to divide pay; Rongjiang had no garrison troops, and the great army pressed deeper still.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yiqing and Yongzuo entered Guilin to divide supplies, leaving Rongjiang undefended, and the Qing armies drove deeper.

sentences.zh: 十一月五日，式耜檄印選出，不肯行，再趣之，則盡室逃。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month Shisi issued orders to Yinxuan to march out; he refused to go, and when urged again his whole household fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month Shisi ordered Yinxuan out; he refused, and when pressed again fled with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 一青及武陵侯楊國棟、綏寧伯蒲纓、寧武伯馬養麟亦逃去。

translations.literal: Yiqing and the Wuling Marquis Yang Guodong, the Suining Earl Pu Ying, and the Ningwu Earl Ma Yanglin also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing, Wuling Marquis Yang Guodong, Suining Earl Pu Ying, and Ningwu Earl Ma Yanglin fled as well.

sentences.zh: 永祚迎降，城中無一兵。

translations.literal: Yongzuo came out to welcome surrender; in the city there was not a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzuo surrendered; not a single soldier remained in the city.

sentences.zh: 式耜端坐府中，家人亦散。

translations.literal: Shisi sat upright in the government hall; his household had also scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi sat upright in the government hall; his family had fled.

sentences.zh: 部將戚良勛請式耜上馬速走，式耜堅不聽，叱退之。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Qi Liangxun asked Shisi to mount a horse and flee quickly; Shisi firmly would not listen and shouted him away.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate general Qi Liangxun urged him to flee on horseback; Shisi refused and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 俄總督張同敞至，誓偕死，乃相對飲酒，一老兵侍。

translations.literal: Shortly Supreme Commander Zhang Tongchang arrived, swore to die together with him, and they then faced each other drinking wine, one old soldier attending.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Supreme Commander Zhang Tongchang arrived, swore to die with him, and the two sat facing each other over wine, attended by one old soldier.

sentences.zh: 召中軍徐高付以敕印，屬馳送王。

translations.literal: He summoned the central army officer Xu Gao, entrusted him with the imperial commission and seal, and charged him to gallop and deliver them to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned central army officer Xu Gao, gave him the imperial commission and seal, and ordered him to ride posthaste to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是夕，兩人秉燭危坐。

translations.literal: That evening the two men held candles and sat upright in solemn stillness.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the two men sat upright by candlelight, awaiting death.

sentences.zh: 黎明，數騎至。

translations.literal: At dawn several horsemen arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn several horsemen arrived.

sentences.zh: 式耜曰：「吾兩人待死久矣」，遂與偕行，至則踞坐於地。

translations.literal: Shisi said: "We two have long awaited death," and then went with them; on arrival they sat with legs sprawled on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi said, "We have long awaited this," and went with them; on arrival they sat defiantly on the ground.

sentences.zh: 諭之降，不聽，幽於民舍。

translations.literal: They were urged to surrender but would not listen and were confined in a common dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Urged to surrender, they refused and were confined in a private house.

sentences.zh: 兩人日賦詩倡和，得百余首。

translations.literal: The two men each day composed poems in responsive exchange, obtaining more than a hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they exchanged poems, producing more than a hundred between them.

sentences.zh: 至閏十一月十有七日，將就刑，天大雷電，空中震擊者三，遠近稱異，遂與同敞俱死。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the intercalary eleventh month, as they were about to be executed, heaven sent great thunder and lightning; three shocks resounded in the air; near and far called it strange, and they then died together with Tongchang.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the intercalary eleventh month, as they were led to execution, thunder crashed three times across the sky; people far and near took it as a marvel, and both were executed.

sentences.zh: 同敞，大學士居正曾孫，事見《居正傳》。

translations.literal: Tongchang was the great-grandson of Grand Secretary Juzheng; his affairs are recorded in the 《Biography of Juzheng》.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchang was the great-grandson of Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng; his story appears in the 《Biography of Juzheng》.

sentences.zh: 時桂林殉難者光祿少卿汪皞投水死。

translations.literal: At the time among those who died for the cause at Guilin was Vice Minister of the Imperial Household Wang Hao, who threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who died for the cause at Guilin was Vice Minister of the Imperial Household Wang Hao, who drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 其破平樂也，守將鎮西將軍朱旻如自剄。

translations.literal: When Pingle was taken, the defending general, the Pacifier of the West Zhu Minru, cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingle fell, its defender, Pacifier of the West Zhu Minru, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 有周震者，官中書舍人，居全州，慷慨尚氣節，武岡失，全州危，震邀文武將吏盟於神，誓死拒守。

translations.literal: There was one Zhou Zhen, an attendant in the Secretariat, who lived at Quanzhou; generous and valuing integrity, when Wugang fell and Quanzhou was in peril Zhen invited civil and military officers to swear an oath before the gods, vowing to die resisting and holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: There was Zhou Zhen, a Secretariat attendant at Quanzhou, a man of generous spirit who prized integrity; when Wugang fell and Quanzhou was threatened, he gathered civil and military officers to swear before the gods that they would die defending the city.

sentences.zh: 條城守事宜，上之留守瞿式耜。

translations.literal: He set forth items for defending the city and submitted them to the garrison commander Qu Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up a plan for the city's defense and submitted it to Qu Shisi, who held the garrison.

sentences.zh: 式耜即題為御史，監全州軍。

translations.literal: Shisi at once nominated him as censor to supervise the army of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi immediately appointed him censor to supervise the Quanzhou army.

sentences.zh: 無何，郝永忠、盧鼎自全州撤兵還桂林。

translations.literal: Before long Hao Yongzhong and Lu Ding withdrew their troops from Quanzhou back to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hao Yongzhong and Lu Ding withdrew their troops from Quanzhou to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 守全諸將議舉城降，震力爭不可，眾怒殺之，全州遂失。

translations.literal: The generals defending Quanzhou deliberated surrendering the city; Zhen argued forcefully that this could not be done; the crowd in anger killed him, and Quanzhou was then lost.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commanders resolved to surrender; Zhen protested fiercely; the mutinous troops killed him, and Quanzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：何騰蛟、瞿式耜崎嶇危難之中，介然以艱貞自守。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: He Tengjiao and Qu Shisi, amid rugged peril and hardship, stood apart in guarding steadfast integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: He Tengjiao and Qu Shisi, amid hardship and peril, held fast to unyielding integrity.

sentences.zh: 雖其設施經畫，未能一睹厥效，要亦時勢使然。

translations.literal: Although in their deployments and plans one could not behold their full effect, this too was owing to the force of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Though their plans never fully bore fruit, that was the force of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 其於鞠躬盡瘁之操，無少虧損，固未可以是為訾議也。

translations.literal: As for their devotion unto death, there was not the slightest diminution; one certainly cannot on this account find fault with them.
translations.idiomatic: Their devotion unto death was never diminished; they cannot be faulted on that score.

sentences.zh: 夫節義必窮而後見，如二人之竭力致死，靡有二心，所謂百折不回者矣。

translations.literal: Integrity and righteousness are seen only after one is driven to extremity; like these two men's exerting their strength unto death without a second thought—they are what is called bending a hundred times yet never breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity shows only at the breaking point; these two gave their utmost unto death without wavering—the true meaning of bending but never breaking.

sentences.zh: 明代二百七十余年養士之報，其在斯乎！

translations.literal: The more than two hundred and seventy years of the Ming nurturing scholars—was not their reward manifest here!
translations.idiomatic: Was not the reward of the Ming's two hundred and seventy years of nurturing scholars manifest here!

sentences.zh: 其在斯乎！

translations.literal: Was it not manifest here!
translations.idiomatic: Was it not manifest here!
